questions.prompt: The distance between A(2,3) and B(5,7) is d. Find d².
Find k if (2k,k-1) lies on the line through (1,2) and (4,5).
questions.explanation: The line is y=x+1; k-1=2k+1 gives k=-2.

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (3,-2) and (-1,4). (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find tanθ where θ is the angle between y=2x+3 and y=-x+5.
Find the line through (2,3) making 45° with the positive x-axis.
questions.explanation: Slope=1: y-3=1(x-2) gives y=x+1.

questions.prompt: A line has intercepts 3 and -4 on the axes. Find its equation.
Find the distance of (2,3) from 3x+4y-12=0. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the area of the triangle formed by x=0, y=0, x+y=5. (enter as a reduced fraction)
questions.explanation: Legs of length 5,5: area=(1/2)(5)(5)=25/2.

questions.prompt: A(1,2), B(3,4), C(5,6) are collinear. Find the common slope.
questions.explanation: Slope of AB = slope of BC = 1.

questions.prompt: Find p if 2x+3y=5, x-y=1, px+2y=3 are concurrent. (enter as a reduced fraction)
questions.explanation: Intersection of the first two lines is (8/5,3/5); substituting gives p=9/8.

questions.prompt: Find the equation of the circle with center (2,-3) and radius 5.
questions.explanation: (x-2)²+(y+3)²=25 expands to this form.

questions.prompt: The center of x²+y²-6x+8y-9=0 is (h,k). Find h+k.
questions.explanation: Completing the square gives center (3,-4), so h+k=-1.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the tangent from (1,2) to x²+y²=4.
questions.explanation: Tangent length = sqrt(1²+2²-4)=sqrt(1)=1.

questions.prompt: Find the circle with diameter endpoints A(1,2) and B(5,6).
questions.explanation: Center (3,4), radius²=8: (x-3)²+(y-4)²=8.

questions.prompt: Find the parabola with focus (2,0) and directrix x=-2.
questions.explanation: a=2, so y²=4ax=8x.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the latus rectum of y²=12x.
questions.explanation: Latus rectum=4a=12.

questions.prompt: Find the vertex of x²=-16y.
questions.explanation: The standard form x²=-4ay has its vertex at the origin.

questions.prompt: Find the eccentricity of x²/25+y²/9=1. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the foci of x²/16+y²/7=1.
questions.explanation: a=4,b=√7,e=sqrt(1-7/16)=3/4, giving foci at (±3,0).

questions.prompt: Find the latus rectum of x²/9+y²/4=1. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the hyperbola with foci (±5,0) and vertices (±3,0).
Find the eccentricity of x²/9-y²/16=1. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the asymptotes of x²/4-y²/9=1.
questions.explanation: a=2,b=3, asymptotes y=±(b/a)x=±3x/2.

questions.prompt: Find the latus rectum of x²/16-y²/9=1. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the center of x²+y²+4x-6y=12.
questions.explanation: Completing squares: (x+2)²+(y-3)²=25, center (-2,3).

questions.prompt: Find the slope of 2x-3y=6. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the line parallel to 3x-4y=7 through (1,2).
questions.explanation: 3x-4y+c=0 through (1,2): 3-8+c=0 gives c=5.

questions.prompt: P(2,3) is the midpoint of A(a,0) and B(0,b). Find a+b.
questions.explanation: a/2=2 gives a=4; b/2=3 gives b=6; a+b=10.

questions.prompt: The line through (1,2),(3,4) is perpendicular to the line through (2,3),(k,5). Find k.
questions.explanation: First slope=1, so the perpendicular slope is -1: (5-3)/(k-2)=-1 gives k=0.

questions.prompt: Find the line through the intersection of 2x+y=5 and x+3y=8, parallel to x-2y=4.
questions.explanation: Intersection is (7/5,11/5). Substituting into x-2y+k=0 gives k=3.

questions.prompt: Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x+4y=7 and 3x+4y=12.
Find the circle through (1,0),(0,1),(0,0).
questions.explanation: Using x²+y²+Dx+Ey=0 and the three points gives D=-1,E=-1.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the chord cut by 3x+4y=15 on x²+y²=25.
questions.explanation: Distance from origin to the line is 3. Chord=2sqrt(25-9)=8.

questions.prompt: Find the condition for y=mx+c to be tangent to x²+y²=a².
questions.explanation: Distance from center to line equals a: |c|/sqrt(1+m²)=a.

questions.prompt: x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 passes through the origin and has center (3,4). Find c.
questions.explanation: Center (-g,-f)=(3,4) gives g=-3,f=-4. Passing through the origin forces c=0.

questions.prompt: Find the tangent to y²=8x at (2,4).
questions.explanation: a=2. Tangent: yy₁=2a(x+x₁) gives 4y=4(x+2), i.e. y=x+2.

questions.prompt: The tangent to y²=4ax at t=1 meets the axis at A. Find the distance from A to the focus.
questions.explanation: Tangent: y=x+a. At y=0, A=(-a,0). Focus=(a,0). Distance=2a.

questions.prompt: Find the latus rectum of x²/16+y²/9=1. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the tangent to x²/25+y²/9=1 at (5/√2,3/√2).
questions.explanation: Tangent: x(5/√2)/25+y(3/√2)/9=1 simplifies to 3x+5y=15√2.

questions.prompt: Find the latus rectum of x²/9-y²/16=1. (enter as a reduced fraction)
Find the tangent to x²/4-y²/9=1 at (4,3√3).
questions.explanation: Tangent: 4x/4-3√3y/9=1 simplifies to x-√3y/3=1.

questions.prompt: An ellipse has eccentricity 3/5 and latus rectum 32/5. Find a².
Find the directrix of y²=16x.
questions.explanation: a=4, directrix x=-a=-4.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the chord of x²+y²=4 cut by y=x+1. (no spaces)
questions.explanation: Distance from origin=1/√2. Chord=2sqrt(4-1/2)=√14.

questions.prompt: Find |slope| of the tangent to x²/16+y²/9=1 at x=2 (y>0). (no spaces)
A line through A(2,1) meets the axes at B,C. If the centroid of triangle OBC is (1,1), find the line's equation.
questions.explanation: Centroid (a/3,b/3)=(1,1) gives a=b=3. Through (2,1): x/3+y/3=1 gives x+y=3.

questions.prompt: Find the locus of a point whose distance from (2,3) is twice its distance from (-1,1).
questions.explanation: Squaring (x-2)²+(y-3)²=4[(x+1)²+(y-1)²] and simplifying gives this equation.

questions.prompt: Lines y=mx and y=-mx are both tangent to x²+y²-2x-2y+1=0. Find m².
questions.explanation: The circle has center (1,1), radius 1. Setting the two tangency conditions equal forces m=0.

questions.prompt: Find the chord of x²+y²=25 whose midpoint is (3,4).
questions.explanation: For a circle centered at the origin, the chord with midpoint (x₁,y₁) is xx₁+yy₁=x₁²+y₁².

questions.prompt: Find the length of the latus rectum of y²=4ax, in terms of a (enter the coefficient of a).
questions.explanation: The latus rectum — the focal chord perpendicular to the axis — always has length 4a.

questions.prompt: Find the condition for y=mx+c to be tangent to y²=4ax.
questions.explanation: Substituting and setting the discriminant to zero: (2mc-4a)²-4m²c²=0 gives c=a/m.

questions.prompt: The tangent at P(2,4) to y²=8x meets the directrix at Q. Find the area of triangle PQS, where S is the focus.
questions.explanation: a=2, S=(2,0), directrix x=-2. Tangent: y=x+2, meeting the directrix at Q=(-2,0). Base SQ=4, height=4, area=8.

questions.prompt: Find the locus of midpoints of chords of x²/25+y²/9=1 parallel to y=2x.
questions.explanation: The diameter conjugate to slope m is y=-(b²/a²m)x; with a²=25,b²=9,m=2 this gives 9x+50y=0.

questions.prompt: Find the normal to x²/16+y²/9=1 at (4cosθ,3sinθ).
questions.explanation: Normal: ax/cosθ-by/sinθ=a²-b²; with a=4,b=3 this gives 4x·secθ-3y·cscθ=7.

questions.prompt: For the ellipse x²+4y²=4, the tangent and normal at P meet the major axis at T,N. Show that OT·ON is the same for every eccentric angle θ, and state that constant value. (enter a single number)
questions.explanation: T=(2secθ,0), N=(2cosθ,0). OT·ON=4secθcosθ=4 for every θ, since secθcosθ=1 always.

questions.prompt: Find the chord of x²/16-y²/9=1 with midpoint (2,3).
questions.explanation: Using T=S₁ for the hyperbola: x/8-y/3=-3/4, which clears to 3x-8y+18=0.

questions.prompt: A hyperbola x²/16-y²/9=1 has asymptotes y=±(3/4)x. Does the point (4,3) lie on this hyperbola? (a short phrase)
questions.answer: No — it lies on the asymptote itself
questions.explanation: Substituting (4,3): 16/16-9/9=1-1=0≠1. In fact (4,3) satisfies y=(3/4)x exactly, so it lies on the asymptote — a hyperbola can never pass through a point on its own asymptote.

questions.prompt: Find the locus of the intersection of perpendicular tangents to y²=4ax.
questions.explanation: This locus is always the parabola's directrix, x=-a.

questions.prompt: A circle x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 passes through the two points of y²=4ax at parameters t=1 and t=2 — i.e. through (a,2a) and (4a,4a). Find c in terms of a,g,f. (no spaces)
questions.explanation: Substituting both points and subtracting the resulting equations gives 27a+6g+4f=0, and back-substituting into either equation gives c=-5a²-2ga-4fa.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the chord of x²/9+y²/4=1 with slope 1, passing through the center. (no spaces)
questions.explanation: Substituting y=x: x²(1/9+1/4)=1 gives x²=36/13. The two intersection points are (±6/√13,±6/√13); their distance is 2√(2·36/13)=12√26/13.

questions.prompt: A hyperbola x²/a²-y²/b²=1 has eccentricity √3 and distance between foci 6. Find a²+b².
questions.explanation: e=√3, 2c=6 gives c=3. From e²=1+b²/a²=3: b²=2a². From c=ae=a√3=3: a=√3, so a²=3, b²=6, and a²+b²=9.

questions.prompt: Find the common chord of x²+y²=16 and x²+y²-8x-6y+24=0.
questions.explanation: Subtracting the equations gives -8x-6y+40=0, i.e. 4x+3y=20.

questions.prompt: A line y=mx+c is tangent to both x²+y²=1 and y²=4x, with c>0. Find c. (no spaces)
questions.explanation: Tangent to the circle: c²=1+m². Tangent to the parabola: c=1/m. Combining gives m⁴+m²-1=0, so m²=(√5-1)/2, and c²=1+m²=(1+√5)/2 (the golden ratio). Taking the positive root gives c=√(2+2√5)/2.

questions.prompt: A variable line through P(2,1) meets the axes at A and B. Find the locus of the foot of the perpendicular from the origin O to AB.
questions.explanation: Writing the line as x/a+y/b=1 through P gives 2/a+1/b=1. The foot of perpendicular from O to this line, expressed via a,b and then eliminating a,b using the constraint, gives x²+y²−2x−y=0.

questions.prompt: Find the minimum value of the sum of the intercepts made on the axes by a line passing through (4,3).
questions.explanation: With intercepts a,b>0 and 4/a+3/b=1, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives (4/a+3/b)(a+b) ≥ (√4+√3)², so a+b ≥ (2+√3)² = 7+4√3.

questions.prompt: Circle x²+y²=4 is tangent to the line y=x+c. Find all possible values of c. (format: ±2√2, no spaces)
questions.explanation: Distance from the origin to x−y+c=0 must equal the radius 2: |c|/√2=2, so |c|=2√2.

questions.prompt: Find the circle orthogonal to x²+y²=1 that passes through (2,0) and (0,2). (format: no spaces)
questions.explanation: For a circle x²+y²+Dx+Ey+F=0 orthogonal to x²+y²=1 (where g₂=f₂=0, c₂=−1), the orthogonality condition gives F=1. Substituting the two given points: D=E=−5/2. So the circle is x²+y²−(5/2)x−(5/2)y+1=0, or cleared of fractions: 2x²+2y²−5x−5y+2=0.

questions.prompt: The chord of contact from point P to the circle x²+y²=25 is tangent to the circle x²+y²=9. Find the locus of P.
questions.explanation: For P(x₁,y₁), the chord of contact is xx₁+yy₁=25. This must be tangent to the smaller circle, so 25/√(x₁²+y₁²)=3, giving x₁²+y₁²=625/9.

questions.prompt: The line y=x+c is a common tangent to the circle x²+y²=1/2 and the parabola y²=4x, with c>0. Find c.
questions.explanation: Any line y=mx+a/m is tangent to y²=4ax. With a=1, m=1: c=1. Checking tangency to the circle: distance from origin to x−y+1=0 is 1/√2, matching the circle's radius √(1/2)=1/√2. Confirmed c=1.

questions.prompt: The tangent at the vertex of y²=4ax is the line x=0. The tangent at point P(at²,2at) meets this vertex tangent at point Q. Find Q in terms of a and t. (format: (0,at), no spaces)
questions.explanation: The tangent at P(at²,2at) is ty=x+at². Setting x=0 (the vertex tangent) gives ty=at², so y=at. Thus Q=(0,at).

questions.prompt: Find the locus of the midpoint of a focal chord of the ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1, where the focus is (ae,0). (format: no spaces)
questions.explanation: For a chord with midpoint (h,k), the equation is hx/a²+ky/b²=h²/a²+k²/b² (the T=S₁ form). Since this chord passes through the focus (ae,0): he/a=h²/a²+k²/b². Replacing (h,k) with (x,y) gives x²/a²+y²/b²=ex/a.

questions.prompt: The tangent to x²/16+y²/9=1 at point P meets the coordinate axes at A and B. Find the minimum possible area of triangle OAB.
questions.explanation: Tangent at (4cosθ,3sinθ): (x cosθ)/4+(y sinθ)/3=1. Intercepts: A=(4/cosθ,0), B=(0,3/sinθ). Area = (1/2)(4/cosθ)(3/sinθ) = 6/(sinθcosθ) = 12/sin(2θ). This is minimized when sin(2θ)=1, giving minimum area 12.

questions.prompt: An ellipse's latus rectum equals half its minor axis. Find e² (the square of the eccentricity).
questions.explanation: Latus rectum = 2b²/a; minor axis = 2b. Setting 2b²/a = (1/2)(2b) = b gives 2b=a, so b²/a²=1/4. Then e²=1−b²/a²=1−1/4=3/4.

questions.prompt: For the hyperbola x²/4−y²/9=1, the tangent at parameter t=1 (using P=(a·sec t, b·tan t)) cuts the two asymptotes at L and M. Find the area of triangle OLM.
questions.explanation: For any hyperbola, the tangent at any point cuts the asymptotes at L,M such that the area of triangle OLM is always ab, regardless of the point chosen. Here ab=2×3=6.

questions.prompt: The tangent to the rectangular hyperbola xy=c² at the point (ct, c/t) meets the coordinate axes at A and B. Find the area of triangle OAB in terms of c.
questions.explanation: The tangent at (ct,c/t) is x/t+ty=2c, giving intercepts A=(2ct,0) and B=(0,2c/t). Area = (1/2)(2ct)(2c/t) = 2c².

questions.prompt: Find the equation of the circle whose diameter is the latus rectum of the parabola y²=8x.
questions.explanation: For y²=8x, a=2, so the latus rectum endpoints are (2,4) and (2,−4). The circle has center (2,0) and radius 4: (x−2)²+y²=16, which expands to x²+y²−4x−12=0.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the common chord of the circles x²+y²=10 and x²+y²−2x−2y−2=0.
questions.explanation: Subtracting the equations gives the radical axis: 2x+2y−8=0, i.e. x+y−4=0. The first circle has center (0,0) and radius √10. Distance from center to this line is 4/√2=2√2, so half the chord length is √(10−8)=√2, giving a full chord length of 2√2 ≈ 2.83.

questions.prompt: A variable circle passes through A(2,3) and cuts the circle x²+y²=4 orthogonally. Find the locus of its center. (enter as an equation, no spaces)
questions.explanation: For center (h,k) and radius r, orthogonality with x²+y²=4 gives r²=h²+k²−4. Since the circle passes through A(2,3): (2−h)²+(3−k)²=r²=h²+k²−4. Expanding and simplifying gives 4h+6k=17, i.e. 2x+3y=17/2.

questions.prompt: The line y=mx is a chord of the parabola y²=4ax. If (p,q) is the midpoint of this chord, find the relation between p and q. (format: no spaces)
questions.explanation: Substituting y=mx into y²=4ax gives x=0 or x=4a/m². The midpoint is (2a/m², 2a/m). Eliminating m: from q=2a/m, m=2a/q, so p=2a/m²=q²/(2a), giving q²=2ap.

questions.prompt: Find the eccentricity of the conic 9x²−16y²−36x+32y−124=0.
questions.explanation: Completing the square: 9(x−2)²−16(y−1)²=144, giving (x−2)²/16−(y−1)²/9=1. This is a hyperbola with a²=16, b²=9, so e²=1+b²/a²=1+9/16=25/16, giving e=5/4=1.25.

questions.prompt: A line xcosα+ysinα=p is tangent to both the ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1 and the hyperbola x²/a²−y²/b²=1 (same a,b). Find p²/a².
questions.explanation: Tangency to the ellipse requires p²=a²cos²α+b²sin²α; tangency to the hyperbola requires p²=a²cos²α−b²sin²α. Equating both forces sinα=0, which gives p²=a². So p²/a²=1.

questions.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of every point from which two perpendicular tangents can be drawn to the parabola y²=8x. (This locus is a vertical line — give its x-value.)
questions.explanation: The locus of points from which perpendicular tangents can be drawn to a parabola is always its directrix. For y²=8x (so a=2), the directrix is x=−a=−2.

questions.prompt: Find the radius of the director circle of the ellipse x²/16+y²/9=1 (the locus of points from which perpendicular tangents can be drawn to the ellipse).
questions.explanation: The director circle of an ellipse is x²+y²=a²+b². Here a²+b²=16+9=25, so the radius is √25=5.

questions.prompt: A variable chord of the ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1 subtends a right angle at the center. Find the distance from the center to this chord, in terms of a and b. (format: no spaces)
questions.explanation: This is a standard result: any chord subtending a right angle at the center of the ellipse stays at a constant distance ab/√(a²+b²) from the center.

questions.prompt: For the ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1, the tangent and normal at point P meet the major axis at T and N. If OT·ON = a²/2, find e² (the square of the eccentricity).
questions.explanation: The tangent at (a cosθ,b sinθ) meets the x-axis at T=(a/cosθ,0). The normal meets it at N=((a²−b²)cosθ/a,0). Their product OT·ON simplifies to a²−b²=a²e², independent of θ. Setting a²e²=a²/2 gives e²=1/2.

questions.prompt: Find y²−x² for the director circle of the hyperbola x²/9−y²/16=1 (the locus of points from which perpendicular tangents can be drawn).
questions.explanation: The director circle of a hyperbola is x²−y²=a²−b². Here a²−b²=9−16=−7, so y²−x²=7.

questions.prompt: Find the minimum distance from a point on the parabola y²=4x to the line x+y+3=0, rounded to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: A point on the parabola is (t²,2t). Its distance to the line is |t²+2t+3|/√2. Minimizing t²+2t+3 (always positive) gives its minimum at t=−1, value 2, so minimum distance = 2/√2 = √2 ≈ 1.41.

questions.prompt: For a hyperbola, the conjugate axis equals half the distance between the foci. Find the eccentricity e. (format: 2/√3, no spaces)
questions.explanation: Conjugate axis = 2b; distance between foci = 2ae. Setting 2b = (1/2)(2ae) = ae gives b² = a²e²/4. Since b²=a²(e²−1): a²(e²−1)=a²e²/4, giving (3/4)e²=1, so e²=4/3 and e=2/√3.

questions.prompt: Find the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola 9x²−16y²=144. (enter as a reduced fraction)
questions.explanation: Dividing by 144 gives the standard form x²/16−y²/9=1, so a=4, b=3. The latus rectum length is 2b²/a = 18/4 = 9/2.

questions.prompt: A chord of the parabola y²=4ax subtends a right angle at the vertex. Find the locus of the chord's midpoint. (format: no spaces)
questions.explanation: For points P(at₁²,2at₁), Q(at₂²,2at₂) with OP⊥OQ, the condition works out to t₁t₂=−4. Writing the midpoint as (h,k) and eliminating t₁,t₂ using t₁t₂=−4 and t₁+t₂=k/a gives the locus y²=2a(x−4a).

questions.prompt: If e₁ and e₂ are the eccentricities of a hyperbola and its conjugate hyperbola, they satisfy 1/e₁²+1/e₂²=1. If e₁=2, find e₂. (format: 2/√3, no spaces)
questions.explanation: 1/4+1/e₂²=1 gives 1/e₂²=3/4, so e₂²=4/3 and e₂=2/√3.

questions.prompt: An ellipse's latus rectum equals the distance between its foci. Find e² + e (where e is the eccentricity), given e²+e−1=0. (enter as a single number)
questions.explanation: Latus rectum = 2b²/a; distance between foci = 2ae. Setting these equal: b²=a²e. Since b²=a²(1−e²): 1−e²=e, giving e²+e−1=0 — and by that equation, e²+e simply equals 1 directly. (Solving further, e=(√5−1)/2, the reciprocal of the golden ratio.)

questions.prompt: Tangents are drawn from the point (4,3) to the ellipse x²/16+y²/9=1. Find the equation of the chord of contact. (format: no spaces)
questions.explanation: First confirm (4,3) is outside the ellipse: 16/16+9/9=2>1, so tangents exist. The chord of contact from (x₁,y₁) is xx₁/a²+yy₁/b²=1. Substituting: 4x/16+3y/9=1, i.e. x/4+y/3=1, which clears to 3x+4y=12.

questions.prompt: Tangents to the parabola y²=4ax at parameters t₁ and t₂ meet at point P. If the chord joining t₁ and t₂ passes through the focus (a,0), find the locus of P (a vertical line — give its equation). (format: x=-a, no spaces)
questions.explanation: Tangents at t₁,t₂ meet at (at₁t₂, a(t₁+t₂)). A focal chord requires t₁t₂=−1. Substituting into the x-coordinate: x=a(−1)=−a for all such P, so the locus is the line x=−a.
